expectations.text: Agency: at least three viable approaches exist (not just board-fight-take)
expectations.evidence: Summary: 'The party must decide whether to negotiate, trade, investigate, or force the issue.' Objective: 'Secure, trade for, or learn the truth... without being forced into a single method.' Six independent leads with different methods (alliance, parley, crew investigation, theft/magic, pressure, information brokering). Line 66: 'Combat is one route, but... is neither inevitable nor optimal.'

expectations.text: Causality: Mave's actions follow from her established want (supernatural confirmation to sell)
expectations.evidence: Line 57: 'She wants supernatural confirmation of the Crown's irregularity so she can decide what to sell and to whom.'

expectations.text: Activity: Mave has a concrete next move if uninterrupted
expectations.evidence: Line 84: 'File her findings and seek a buyer. Approach a known intelligence broker, neutral faction, or rival to the Crown.'

expectations.text: Connectivity: multiple leads point to the intercept from different directions
expectations.evidence: Six leads with genuinely different vectors: alliance against Crown, parley via intelligence trade, crew investigation of chip removal, theft via magic/divination, pressure via Crown patrol, information market interception.

expectations.text: Gravity: the chip connects to an existing PC interest or campaign thread
expectations.evidence: Connects to Wardstone ritual split, Crown supernatural irregularity, Dravosi Crown faction.

expectations.text: Persistence: outcomes name lasting world changes
expectations.evidence: Fallout names ledger records of party identity, chip holder tracked by Crown diviners, Wardstone gap detection, potential network contact status.

expectations.text: Vault integrity: named entities resolve to existing wiki pages
expectations.evidence: Mave Sorn, Velvet Noose, Magistrate's Warding Chip, Dravosi Crown, Central Strait Crossing, Kalowe all resolve.

expectations.text: Quest frame sentence names incompatible wants, live pressure, and uninterrupted consequence
expectations.evidence: Summary names Mave's want (supernatural confirmation to sell), the pressure (open water, Crown attention), and what happens uninterrupted (Mave files and sells). Frame is situation-first, not prescriptive.

expectations.text: Walk-away entry names what continues without the party
expectations.evidence: Line 73: 'The intercept remains unresolved. Mave files the irregularity and seeks a buyer. The chip stays with her unless another force intercepts it later.'
